A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedRE research. All 15 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, representation-inversion results, communication measurements, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments examining performance with small numbers of clients.

M1.justification: Local training, representation mapping, weighted representation/label entanglement, global-classifier training, and broadcast remain unchanged. AP and RAP remain the defaults. Algorithm 1 is rewritten without changing its operations.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and the synthetic two-dimensional classification data. The added small-client study varies client counts within existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in retained experiments is unchanged. The new client-count study reuses FedAvg, FedProto, and FedGH from the existing homogeneous comparison. Newly discussed FedMP, FedGPS, and FedPhoenix are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 adds evaluations with 2 and 4 homogeneous four-layer CNN clients alongside the existing 10-client setting. Retained experiments keep their protocols; the 75%/25% split restates v1's 3:1 split.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.2 and Table 12 test sensitivity to having few clients on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Existing mapping, entanglement, weight-distribution, resampling, runtime, and statistical-heterogeneity analyses are retained, including relocated appendix material.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random experiments and standard deviations for the main accuracy comparisons. The new client-count table reports point estimates, consistent with existing sensitivity tables; no new uncertainty procedure or revised run count is reported.

E6.justification: Table 12 adds results for 2 and 4 clients. With 2 clients on CIFAR-100, FedRE scores 41.57%, versus FedGH's 39.61%, FedProto's 37.87%, and FedAvg's 33.13%. Matched existing accuracy, privacy, communication, and ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B newly formalizes the inversion objective and specifies a semi-honest server with full extractor access. The explicit Mixup/Beta formulation becomes a verbal comparison. Core RE definitions and complexity remain equivalent; the new convergence discussion provides no theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: entangled representations, a flexible FedRE framework, and a trade-off among accuracy, privacy protection, and communication overhead. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.3.3 explicitly acknowledges that rigorous non-convex convergence analysis remains future work, citing classifier replacement and entanglement as complications. Appendix C.2 newly attributes declining accuracy with fewer clients to reduced diversity of the transmitted representations.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds attacker access, fixed-noise inversion, the reconstruction objective, and the common CNN extractor setup. Conversely, v2 omits the CPU specification, CUDA/PyTorch/Python versions, and the explicit 512-dimensional mapping statement. GPU and code-access information remain available.

R1.justification: v2 adds FedMP, FedGPS, FedPhoenix, and two incremental/category-discovery FL references, while removing the prototype-similarity-distillation reference. Section 3.3.2 makes comparisons with existing FL methods more explicit without fundamentally changing the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 polishes wording, rewrites Algorithm 1 in prose, reorganizes Section 3.3, and consolidates the homogeneous-setting discussion in a reordered Appendix C. The overall narrative and main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with explicit upload/broadcast arrows, and Figure 2's colorbar and caption are revised. v2 adds the client-count table, removes two setup-table rows, and relocates several existing appendix displays. Most display designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The small-client study adds useful sensitivity evidence, and the explicit attack setup makes the privacy evaluation easier to assess. The convergence qualification and revised diagram improve clarity. These modest gains outweigh the loss of some environment and representation-dimension details, while the method and principal empirical evidence remain unchanged.
